description: Part 2a: Bring the stale frontend/e2e Playwright specs and shared helpers in line with the REAL current UI so they pass against the running app. The specs currently drive through helpers.ts::commitSelectedScan, which uses UI that no longer exists (a `Select for batch review` checkbox, a `Direction` select via getByLabel('Direction').selectOption(...), and a `Commit 1 selected` button). The current UI instead uses: per-card `Approve`(exact)/`Remove` buttons, a `Select scan for batch approval` checkbox, and stamps direction from the scanner MODE (an on-screen `Mode: stock_in`/`Mode: stock_out` banner) - switching to stock_out is done by scanning the STOCK_OUT control barcode, NOT a per-scan Direction dropdown or the view Tabs. Ground every selector in the actual current frontend source (already read: ScanQueuePage.tsx, ScanEntryCard.tsx, FlaggedEntryResolver.tsx, StockOutInstanceSelector.tsx, InventoryPage.tsx, ItemInstanceList.tsx, SuggestionPanel.tsx, ShoppingListPage.tsx) and in the proven driver .agents/skills/verify-pantry/scripts/drive-stock-in.mjs. Do NOT weaken assertions to make them pass; fix the selectors/flow. This must run BEFORE FEAT-002/003 because it establishes the confirmed selectors.
steps: Install Playwright's Chromium for the frontend once so specs can run: `cd frontend && npx playwright install chromium` (OPEN_INTERNET is available; browser binaries persist in $HOME).

Rewrite frontend/e2e/helpers.ts::commitSelectedScan to use the REAL flow. It currently checks a `Select for batch review` checkbox, calls getByLabel('Direction').selectOption(direction), optionally fills `Expiration date`, then clicks `Commit 1 selected` and asserts the card is gone. Replace with the per-card single-approve flow demonstrated in drive-stock-in.mjs: (a) if an expirationDate is provided, fill the card's `Expiration date` input via scanCard.getByLabel('Expiration date').fill(expirationDate) and blur/commit it (the field patches on blur; press Tab or click elsewhere so the PATCH fires before approving); (b) click scanCard.getByRole('button', { name: 'Approve', exact: true }); (c) await expect(scanCard).toHaveCount(0) (card detaches after commit). The `direction` parameter is no longer set per-scan through the card - direction comes from the scanner mode at scan time. Decide the cleanest signature: either drop the `direction` argument entirely (callers already scan in the correct mode) OR keep it only to assert/guard, but do NOT try to set a Direction control that no longer exists. Update the JSDoc/comment to describe the real flow.

Add a helper to switch the scanner into stock_out mode the way a user does: scan the STOCK_OUT control barcode. Because a control barcode does NOT create a scan card (ScanQueuePage.captureBarcode returns early after calling setScannerMode), a card-waiting helper like scanBarcode will hang. Add e.g. `setScannerMode(page, 'stock_out')` (or `scanControlBarcode`) that fills the `Barcode scanner input` textbox with 'STOCK_OUT', presses Enter, and awaits the banner: await expect(page.getByText('Mode: stock_out')).toBeVisible(). Provide the stock_in equivalent if a spec needs to switch back. Confirm the exact control-barcode strings from GET /api/scanner/config (defaults STOCK_IN/STOCK_OUT, already confirmed).

Fix frontend/e2e/stock-in.spec.ts: the card assertions (Barcode: <barcode>, /^Scanned:/) are still valid. Replace the `commitSelectedScan(page, scanCard, 'stock_in', '2030-06-15')` call with the updated helper flow. Confirm the queue is in stock_in mode first (default; optionally assert `Mode: stock_in`). Keep the inventory assertions (`1 carton`) intact.

Fix frontend/e2e/flagged-resolution.spec.ts: it scans an unseeded barcode, asserts the `Flagged` badge, fills the `Create new product` fieldset (Product name/Category/Unit of measure), clicks `Create and use product`, then asserts Flagged is gone, the product heading appears, and a `Select scan for batch approval` checkbox appears. Those selectors are correct against FlaggedEntryResolver/ScanEntryCard. Replace the trailing `commitSelectedScan(page, scanCard, 'stock_in', '2031-03-20')` with the updated helper flow so the resolved card is approved via the per-card Approve button. Note: a resolved flagged entry has direction still null until stamped - verify from source (ScanEntryCard only shows Approve/Remove when entry.status==='pending' && entry.direction !== null). If a resolved entry's direction is null, the Approve button will not render; in that case the spec should scan in stock_in mode first so the created scan carries a direction, or assert resolution only (flag cleared + approvable checkbox) matching the flagged-resolution recipe's 'stop once the flag is cleared' option. Choose the approach that reflects real behavior; do NOT invent selectors. If approval is not reachable for a resolved entry, keep the spec asserting the resolution outcome (Flagged cleared, product heading, batch checkbox) which is already the documented deliverable.

Fix frontend/e2e/stock-out-oldest.spec.ts: it stocks two instances (2030-01-10, 2030-12-20) then scans in stock_out. Update the two stock-in commits to the new helper (each sets the card's Expiration date then Approve). For the stock-out scan, first switch to stock_out mode via the new control-barcode helper (assert `Mode: stock_out`), THEN scan the product (a stock-out card appears under the Stock out view), leave the StockOutInstanceSelector at the default `Use oldest available automatically` (empty value) to exercise oldest-first, and Approve. The inventory assertions (`1 box`, View instances, `Expires Dec 20, 2030` visible, `Expires Jan 10, 2030` count 0) are grounded in ItemInstanceList's medium/UTC formatDate and are correct - keep them. Note the ItemRow toggle button is `View instances`.

Fix frontend/e2e/shopping-list.spec.ts: it stocks two units, sets a target quantity of 2 via Get suggestion -> Manual target quantity -> Save manual target (asserting `Target quantity set to 2.`), stocks out one unit to create a shortfall, then on Shopping List expects a `Derived` row with `1 bag` and clicks `Mark <product> purchased`. CRITICAL from source: derived (auto) entries have an empty id and render NO action buttons (they show 'Updates when inventory changes'); the `Mark <product> purchased` button only exists for manual/materialized entries. So the current step that clicks Mark purchased on the Derived row will fail against the real UI. Reconcile with real behavior per the shopping-list feature recipe: keep asserting the Derived row appears with the shortfall quantity and Derived badge (that is the derivation proof), and for the purchase/remove interaction use a Manual entry: add the product via the `Add an item` form (Pantry item select + Quantity + `Add to shopping list`), then `Mark <product> purchased` and assert the manual row leaves the list. Preserve the assertion that inventory is unchanged by a purchase (readInventory/inventory row count unchanged). Update the stock-out step to use the control-barcode mode switch helper. Do NOT weaken the derived-shortfall assertion.

Ensure the e2e specs can run in one shell invocation. frontend/playwright.config.ts already declares a webServer that boots `go run ../cmd/server` (API on 127.0.0.1:18080, DISABLE_EXTERNAL_PRODUCT_LOOKUP=true, tmp DB) and `npm run dev` (Vite). Running `npx playwright test` starts both, runs specs, and tears down in a single process, satisfying the sandbox constraint. If the webServer needs a tweak (e.g. explicit port/strictPort or a longer timeout) to be reliable, make the minimal change; otherwise leave it. Keep DISABLE_EXTERNAL_PRODUCT_LOOKUP=true so seeded overrides drive scans and unseeded barcodes flag.

Run the full e2e suite from frontend/: `npx playwright test` and confirm all four specs pass. If a selector still misses, re-read the specific component source and fix the selector - never delete or soften an assertion to get green. Iterate until green.
Run the frontend gate to confirm no regressions: `cd frontend && npx tsc -b && npm run lint && npx vitest --run` all pass (helpers.ts is TypeScript and is type-checked/linted).
acceptance_criteria: frontend/e2e/helpers.ts no longer references `Select for batch review`, `getByLabel('Direction')`, or `Commit 1 selected`; it uses per-card Approve (exact) + Expiration date + `Select scan for batch approval` and a control-barcode mode-switch helper, all grounded in current source.
Running `cd frontend && npx playwright test` passes all four specs (stock-in, flagged-resolution, stock-out-oldest, shopping-list) against the app booted by the config's webServer.
No assertion was weakened or deleted to achieve green: the derived-shortfall, oldest-first-expiry, inventory-count, and target-quantity assertions remain present and meaningful.
`cd frontend && npx tsc -b && npm run lint && npx vitest --run` all pass.
verification: cd frontend && npx playwright install chromium
cd frontend && npx playwright test  (all four specs green)
cd frontend && npx tsc -b && npm run lint && npx vitest --run
findings:
Done. Rewrote frontend/e2e/helpers.ts and all four specs against the REAL current UI (grounded in ScanEntryCard/ScanQueuePage/FlaggedEntryResolver/StockOutInstanceSelector/ShoppingListPage/handler_shopping_list_get.go). helpers.ts now: scanBarcode (unchanged), setScannerMode (scans STOCK_IN/STOCK_OUT control barcode, waits for `Mode: <mode>` banner), resetToStockIn (per-run mode reset), commitSelectedScan (fills card Expiration date + Tab-to-blur, clicks per-card Approve exact, asserts card detaches - no more `Select for batch review`, `getByLabel('Direction')`, or `Commit 1 selected`).

Key findings during implementation:
1) Scanner mode is SERVER-SIDE GLOBAL state that persists for the whole `npx playwright test` run (one webServer + one DB, workers:1). A spec that switched to stock_out leaked into later specs. Fix: added resetToStockIn(page) at the top of every spec after page.goto('/'); it waits for the mode banner to settle then scans STOCK_IN only if not already stock_in. No config change to playwright.config.ts was needed.
2) stock-out: after switching to stock_out and scanning, must wait for the StockOutInstanceSelector radio `Use oldest available automatically` to render (inventory item mapping loads async) before clicking Approve; approving too early sends a commit with no item and errors `no item found`. The stock-out spec now waits for that radio, then approves, leaving default (empty value) to exercise oldest-first.
3) SHOPPING LIST derived-entry premise correction: the backend materializes derived entries via shopping.SyncDerivedItems (auto_items.go), so the Derived/auto shortfall row carries a REAL id and DOES render `Mark <product> purchased`/`Remove` buttons (ShoppingListPage renders buttons when entry.id !== ''). The empty-id/no-buttons case only applies to the frontend-only pure fallback deriveShoppingListEntries(), not the API-backed list the page shows. So the manual-entry detour was unnecessary; the spec keeps the Derived-shortfall assertion (Derived badge + `1 bag`, target 2 - 1 on hand) intact and exercises purchase by marking the derived row purchased directly. Marking it purchased dismisses it (purchased gaps stay hidden until quantity changes) and leaves inventory unchanged (still `1 bag`) - all real behavior, no assertion weakened.

Proof (all green):
- `cd frontend && npx playwright test` => 4 passed (flagged-resolution, shopping-list, stock-in, stock-out-oldest), reproduced twice in fresh shells.
- `cd frontend && npx tsc -b` => clean.
- `cd frontend && npm run lint` (eslint .) => clean.
- `cd frontend && npx vitest --run` => 20 files, 157 tests passed.
